cues: On a neighborhood commute, steady pedaling can bypass traffic queues and leave a rider close to the office entrance.
A dropped chain beside the curb can interrupt a trip until the rider reseats it on the front chainring.
After a flat tire, a rider may patch the inner tube at a roadside stop before continuing home.
A U-shaped lock secures the frame to a rack outside shops while its owner runs errands.
On steep city streets, low gearing makes each pedal stroke easier, though the climb takes longer.
A helmet and bright rear light help commuters remain visible during a rainy ride home after dusk.
At a weekend market, a small rear basket carries groceries while the rider balances along neighborhood lanes.
During a group ride, volunteers mark a route with water stops and repair stations for tired participants.
